questions.question: What is the main difference between belief and unbelief in this passage?
questions.answer: Belief is knowing and saying yes to truth, while unbelief is mostly denial and not knowing.

questions.question: If unbelief looks like it is saying something, what is it really like in the passage?
questions.answer: It is really more like rejecting and emptying out truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say every denying side of belief can lead to?
questions.answer: It can lead to a real and good truth.

questions.question: When people try very hard to accept a false negative idea as true, how is that described?
questions.answer: It is treated as a wrong kind of knowledge or a mistaken judgment.

questions.question: What is easier than building a false belief against faith?
questions.answer: Simply refusing to accept the truth.

questions.question: What is simple refusal to accept called in the passage?
questions.answer: It is called ignorance.

questions.question: How many main kinds of unbelief are named?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: What is the first main kind of unbelief like?
questions.answer: It has its own false ideas and wrong judgment, but it is not the kind being discussed here.

questions.question: What does the second main kind of unbelief do?
questions.answer: It fights against the truths of faith.

questions.question: What are the two parts of this second kind?
questions.answer: One is not accepting, and the other is accepting non-being.

questions.question: Which part has no real judgment in it?
questions.answer: Not accepting.

questions.question: Which part includes a heart decision and taking a side?
questions.answer: Accepting non-being.

questions.question: Why does that second part have to support its denial?
questions.answer: Because it has chosen a side and made a judgment.

questions.question: What is one kind of negation that can be proved?
questions.answer: Saying a certain thing is not in one certain place or direction.

questions.question: What kind of denial cannot be proved?
questions.answer: Denial of big faith matters about the world, all beings, the Hereafter, and time.

questions.question: Why can that big denial not be proved?
questions.answer: Because a person would need to see everything everywhere and every time.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the core of unbelief that fights Islam?
questions.answer: It is built on denial, lack of knowledge, and saying no.

questions.question: How is belief described in a good way?
questions.answer: It is described as knowledge, truth, and saying yes.

questions.question: If a person rejects faith without even accepting a clear wrong idea, what is that called?
questions.answer: It is called complete ignorance.

questions.question: What short summary is given before the kinds of unbelief are listed?
questions.answer: That there are two kinds of convictions under unbelief.

questions.question: Does the first kind of unbelief mainly battle the truths of Islam, or does it keep its own false ideas?
questions.answer: It keeps its own false ideas.

questions.question: Is the first kind the focus of this discussion?
questions.answer: No, it is not the focus.

questions.question: Which kind is the focus of this discussion?
questions.answer: The kind that opposes belief and struggles against it.

questions.question: What is the first variety inside that opposing kind?
questions.answer: Just not accepting the truth.

questions.question: Why is simple non-acceptance easier to fall into?
questions.answer: Because it does not require a real judgment.

questions.question: What is the second variety inside that opposing kind?
questions.answer: Accepting non-being.

questions.question: What part of the person agrees with that second variety?
questions.answer: The heart.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying a judgment is involved?
questions.answer: The person has chosen a belief and taken a side.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation about?
questions.answer: It is about saying something is not in one certain place.

questions.question: Is that first type inside or outside the main discussion?
questions.answer: It is outside the main discussion.

questions.question: What does the second type of negation try to deny?
questions.answer: It tries to deny broad sacred teachings about this world, all creation, the Hereafter, and different times.

questions.question: What would someone need in order to prove that broad denial?
questions.answer: They would need unlimited sight over the whole universe, the Hereafter, and all time.

questions.question: In this passage, which is stronger and fuller: belief or unbelief?
questions.answer: Belief.

questions.question: Why is belief shown as stronger?
questions.answer: Because it has knowledge, affirmation, and true judgment.

questions.question: Why is unbelief shown as weak?
questions.answer: Because it rests on denial and not knowing.

questions.question: Can unbelief sometimes look like a belief?
questions.answer: Yes, but inside it is still a kind of rejection.

questions.question: If someone holds a wrong idea and accepts it as true, what does the passage call that?
questions.answer: A mistaken judgment.

questions.question: If someone merely refuses truth without a settled judgment, what does the passage call that?
questions.answer: Ignorance.

questions.question: What is one way the first kind of unbelief is different from the second kind?
questions.answer: The first has its own false acceptance, while the second pushes against the truths of faith.

questions.question: Which kind would be more active in fighting belief?
questions.answer: The second kind.

questions.question: In the second kind, what is the simpler variety?
questions.answer: Not accepting.

questions.question: What makes that simpler variety less firm?
questions.answer: It does not include a true judgment.

questions.question: What makes acceptance of non-being more serious?
questions.answer: It includes heart agreement and choosing a side.

questions.question: What does “taking the part of something” mean here?
questions.answer: It means siding with denial.

questions.question: What is an example of a denial that can be checked and proved?
questions.answer: Saying something is not in one certain place.

questions.question: Why is denying all big sacred truths much harder to prove?
questions.answer: Because those truths are wide and cover all creation and time.

questions.question: What does the passage say unbelief is made of at its root?
questions.answer: Denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What does the passage say belief is made of at its root?
questions.answer: Knowledge, affirmation, and judgment.

questions.question: How can something that seems like a positive belief still be unbelief?
questions.answer: If it is really built on rejecting truth, it is still unbelief.

questions.question: When false denial is accepted like a belief, is it called sound knowledge or mistaken knowledge?
questions.answer: Mistaken knowledge.

questions.question: When a person does not accept and does not admit, is that described as a judgment or as no judgment?
questions.answer: No judgment.

questions.question: What are the two big kinds of unbelief convictions listed in the passage?
questions.answer: One ignores the truths of Islam, and one opposes them.

questions.question: Why is the first big kind not the main topic here?
questions.answer: Because the passage says it is outside this discussion.

questions.question: What are the two smaller varieties inside the unbelief that opposes faith?
questions.answer: Non-acceptance and acceptance of non-being.

questions.question: Which of those two is called a kind of ignorance?
questions.answer: Non-acceptance.

questions.question: Which of those two needs inner approval from the heart?
questions.answer: Acceptance of non-being.

questions.question: What follows after a person gives heart approval to denial?
questions.answer: The person must defend that denial.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation mentioned after that?
questions.answer: Denying something in one limited place or direction.

questions.question: Why is that first type different from the second type?
questions.answer: Because the first can be proved, but the second cannot.

questions.question: What large areas does the second type try to deny?
questions.answer: This world, all beings, the Hereafter, and the flow of ages.

questions.question: What would make proving that second type impossible for a human being?
questions.answer: No human can see all places, all beings, the Hereafter, and all time.

questions.question: Which side in the passage is linked with real knowing?
questions.answer: Belief.

questions.question: Which side is linked with simply saying no?
questions.answer: Unbelief.

questions.question: If someone says no to truth without careful proof, what does the passage connect that with?
questions.answer: Ignorance.

questions.question: What does the passage say about unbelief that only seems like a real belief?
questions.answer: It may look real, but truly it is still negation.

questions.question: What happens if people force themselves to accept a false denial as true?
questions.answer: It becomes a wrong judgment in one way.

questions.question: What is even easier than making that wrong judgment?
questions.answer: Just refusing to accept the truth.

questions.question: How many kinds of unbelief convictions are described before more details are given?
questions.answer: Two kinds.

questions.question: What is special about the first kind?
questions.answer: It has its own baseless belief and is not the subject here.

questions.question: What is special about the second kind?
questions.answer: It stands against belief and argues with it.

questions.question: Which variety under the second kind is only a lack of agreement?
questions.answer: Non-acceptance.

questions.question: Which variety under the second kind is an inner choice for denial?
questions.answer: Acceptance of non-being.

questions.question: Why is acceptance of non-being more than simple confusion?
questions.answer: Because it includes belief in denial and choosing its side.

questions.question: What is the narrow kind of denial that can be shown?
questions.answer: Denying one thing in one set place or direction.

questions.question: What is the wide kind of denial that cannot be shown?
questions.answer: Denying broad sacred truths about all creation and the Hereafter.

questions.question: What would a person have to do to prove that wide denial?
questions.answer: The person would have to know everything in the universe and beyond time.

questions.question: What three words best describe the base of unbelief in the passage?
questions.answer: Denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What three ideas are used for belief in the passage?
questions.answer: Knowledge, affirmation, and judgment.

questions.question: Does the passage present belief as empty or as something real and full?
questions.answer: Something real and full.

questions.question: What may a negative side of belief be covering?
questions.answer: A positive truth.

questions.question: When can unbelief be counted as a mistaken kind of knowing?
questions.answer: When people try to accept a false negation as if it were true.

questions.question: What is non-acceptance called when there is no real judgment in it?
questions.answer: Absolute ignorance.

questions.question: What are the two main classes of unbelief named in the summary?
questions.answer: One that does not care for Islamic truths, and one that fights them.

questions.question: What does the passage say about our concern with the first class?
questions.answer: It says that class is not the one being discussed.

questions.question: What are the two varieties in the class that fights belief?
questions.answer: Not accepting and accepting non-being.

questions.question: Which variety happens easily?
questions.answer: Not accepting.

questions.question: Why does it happen easily?
questions.answer: Because it does not require a settled judgment.

questions.question: What extra step exists in accepting non-being?
questions.answer: The heart agrees with denial.

questions.question: What result comes from that extra step?
questions.answer: The person becomes committed to defending the denial.

questions.question: Which type of negation is limited and provable?
questions.answer: Denial about one thing in one place or direction.

questions.question: Which type of negation is broad and unprovable?
questions.answer: Denial of major sacred truths that cover the world, beings, the Hereafter, and time.

questions.question: What kind of sight would be needed to prove that broad denial?
questions.answer: A sight that reaches the whole universe, the Hereafter, and every time.
